angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 221,233 km at 86.23 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.5973 +/- 0.0164 mas (same row, RUWE 1.15): 86.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.318 +/- 0.033 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-89 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 221,233 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.347 +/- 0.036 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-89 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3691 +/- 51 K from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-89 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-89 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-89.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.974, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
